name: Islandbridge
facts: In 1787, a flood swept away the original stone bridge at Island Bridge, prompting a swift reconstruction between 1791 and 1793 that introduced the single 32‑metre ashlar masonry elliptical arch still admired today.

When the new span opened, the Countess of Westmorland, Sarah Fane, laid the first stone on 22 June 1791, and the bridge was christened Sarah's Bridge before adopting its current name after independence.
Archaeologists have uncovered Viking burial sites from the 9th and 10th centuries near Island Bridge, marking the area as one of the earliest documented contacts between Norse raiders and Ireland.
